## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit identified a critical problem with the effluent pump. The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate current, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a failure condition requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components measured within normal parameters during this visit.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter was light with soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this maintenance visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Load % | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | 22.2% | CRITICAL |

**Finding:** The pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated full-load amperage. This indicates the pump motor is operating without hydraulic load -- the pump is spinning but not moving fluid. This is a failure condition.

**Probable Causes:**
- The impeller is broken or missing.
- The discharge line is severed or disconnected.
- The pump is running dry (no fluid in the pump housing).

**Risk:** A motor running without fluid cooling will overheat and fail rapidly. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**Electrical Connections:** Sound. High water alarm tested and functional.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
Surface condition is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (Critical):**
- Stop operating the pump. Immediate professional attention is required to diagnose the cause of the no-load condition. A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or damage, and must check the impeller for breakage or displacement. Do not run the pump again until the cause has been identified and corrected.

**Secondary (Routine):**
- Once the pump is repaired or replaced, measure dissolved oxygen in the aerobic treatment unit to establish treatment effectiveness. Dissolved oxygen was not measured during this maintenance visit and is necessary to confirm the aerobic system is functioning.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

Your septic system is an aerobic treatment unit, which means it relies on a pump to move treated effluent from the tank to the dispersal field. During this maintenance visit, the pump was found to be running but not pumping -- it is drawing far less electrical current than it should, which means it is not moving fluid.

This is not a minor wear issue. The pump must be examined by a qualified technician immediately. The most likely causes are a broken impeller inside the pump, a disconnected discharge pipe, or the pump running dry. Running the pump in this condition will damage the motor.

Your tank itself is in good condition. Solids are accumulating at a normal rate. The filter is clean. But the pump must be fixed before your system can work properly.
